meta_desc: NCERT Exemplar Class 12 Q27 solved: evaluate the definite integral of x squared plus 3 from 0 to 2 as a limit of a sum, plus a free 8-question quiz.

quiz.title: Definite Integral as a Limit of a Sum Quiz
quiz.intro: Eight questions on the first-principles definition of the definite integral, using this NCERT Exemplar problem as the anchor. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.
quiz.about: Definite integral as the limit of a sum (Class 12 integration)

questions.q: In the limit-of-a-sum definition ∫₀² f(x)dx, what is the width h of each subinterval when [0, 2] is split into n equal parts?
Using right endpoints on [0, 2] with n parts, what is the sample point xᵢ for the i-th rectangle?
For f(x) = x² + 3 on [0, 2], the term f(xᵢ)h equals which expression?
Which formula for the sum of the first n squares is needed in this problem?
questions.explanation: Σi² = 1² + 2² + ... + n² = n(n+1)(2n+1)/6. The sum of the first n natural numbers, n(n+1)/2, is not required here.

questions.q: As n → ∞, the limit of (2n+1)(n+1)/n² equals what value?
What is the exact value of ∫₀² (x² + 3) dx?
questions.explanation: The limit of the sum gives 8/3 + 6 = 26/3. Checking by antiderivative: [x³/3 + 3x]₀² = 8/3 + 6 = 26/3.

questions.q: Verifying by the Fundamental Theorem, the term 3x in the antiderivative of x² + 3 contributes how much over [0, 2]?
questions.explanation: The antiderivative of the constant 3 is 3x, and [3x]₀² = 3(2) − 3(0) = 6. The x² part contributes 8/3.

questions.q: In the definition ∫ᾚᵇ f(x)dx = lim h[f(a) + f(a+h) + ... + f(a+(n-1)h)], what does 'nh' equal?
questions.explanation: Since h = (b − a)/n, we get nh = b − a. This keeps the total length of the interval fixed as n grows.

faq.q: What does it mean to evaluate an integral 'as a limit of a sum'?
faq.a: It means computing the definite integral straight from its first-principles definition rather than using an antiderivative. You split the interval into n equal strips, add the areas of the rectangles, and take the limit as n tends to infinity so the strips become infinitely thin.

faq.q: Why is the sum-of-squares formula needed for this problem?
faq.a: Because f(x) = x² + 3 has a squared term, the Riemann sum contains Σi². Replacing it with the closed form n(n+1)(2n+1)/6 turns the sum into an algebraic expression in n that you can take the limit of.

faq.q: What is the final answer to ∫₀²(x²+3)dx?
faq.a: The value is 26/3. The x² part contributes 8/3 and the constant 3 contributes 6 over the interval [0, 2], giving 8/3 + 6 = 26/3.

faq.q: How can I check the limit-of-a-sum answer quickly?
faq.a: Use the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus: the antiderivative of x² + 3 is x³/3 + 3x, and evaluating [x³/3 + 3x] from 0 to 2 gives 8/3 + 6 = 26/3. Matching this value confirms your limit calculation was correct.
